Fixed anchors: A = continuous laminate counter, metal rim and solid wood base, with stools on customer side; B = rectangular rear kitchen hatch; C = coffee-machine wall/back worktop on service side; D = front/side windows and booth row on customer side. A-D establish physical sides despite reverse angles.
Entities: W = gray-haired woman in blue shirt and white apron; M = gray-haired man in brown jacket. Not visible means outside the frame or unresolved unless the expected location is shown empty.
State shot 1: W and M not reliably identifiable through distant windows; sides of A/B/C and actions unresolved; camera outside D.
State shot 2: W present between A and C, dining-room side of B, opposite D across A; faces down toward A and wipes with right hand while moving along service aisle. M not visible.

State shot 3: W remains between A/C, facing A and then M; wipes and raises coffee pot in right hand. M appears near rear doorway/B, visibly rounds rear counter end, walks between A and D, then sits on customer-side stool facing W/C.

State shot 4: M's brown-sleeved hands visible from customer side of A; he releases mug onto A. W's arm and apron visible from service/C side, pouring with right hand. Faces, B and D mostly cropped; no hand/person substitution.
State shot 5: Neither person visible in tight food insert; A surface and distant D booths visible; B/C outside frame. Body positions and facing cannot be determined.

State shot 6: M present at front counter bend with mug held in both hands, facing down room toward camera; torso lies on C/service side of A while visible jeans-clad leg lies outside A's solid base toward stools/D. B behind him. W not visible in shown service aisle.

State shot 7: W present immediately on dining-room side of B, between A/C, facing hatch and wiping with right hand, then turning toward M. M present farther toward front/D at A with mug, facing counter. Reverse camera explains screen-side reversal.
State shot 8: Neither person visible; area around B and service aisle between A/C shown empty, front seating cropped. Increasing exterior light at D indicates a temporal transition.

State shot 9: M present on stool between A and D near B end, facing C/down toward mug. W present between A/C, initially facing C while working, then turns and approaches M along service aisle with dishes.

State shot 10: M remains customer/D side of A, seated facing W/C, lifting and setting mug with right hand. W remains service/C side of A in front of B, handles plate and mug, then turns toward B carrying plate.

State shot 11: M remains customer-side stool near B, facing A/C with mug. W moves from service side toward rear/B end of A and onto customer side, sits beside M nearer B, faces A/C with mug; her route is shown rather than an unexplained cut relocation.

State shot 12: Both present together on customer/D side of A, W nearer B and M nearer front; D behind them and C behind camera. Both hold mugs, M turns toward W. Reverse view preserves their physical order.
State shot 13: Neither person visible in rear A/B/C framing; stronger sunlight and an empty-room insert allow elapsed time, while front seating is cropped.

State shot 14: Brown-sleeved hands consistent with M place money beside mug on A and withdraw; body/facing and B/C/D relationships cropped. W not visible; no across-cut continuation by another identifiable person or hand.

State shot 15: M present outside D, back toward diner, walks toward truck cab. W visible only as reflection in D, inside diner facing outward. A/B/C outside frame; reflection is not a duplicate person.

State shot 16: W present beside D/booth, facing outside toward M, then turns inward. M remains outside D at truck cab, reaches toward door. W's window reflection accompanies her actual body; A/B/C outside frame.

State shot 17: W initially seated customer/D side of A facing C, then rises with mugs. Around 01:52 her torso enters service side of A while a leg remains through its solid base on stool side; by 01:53 she stands at C. Simultaneously a second matching W wipes A beside B from about 01:52-01:55. M not visible, consistent with preceding exterior departure.
Diff 1->2: exterior-to-interior framing reveals W; distant exterior does not establish her absence.
Diff 2->3: W retains service side of A; M's entrance and path around rear end are visible.
Diff 3->4: seated M and W's right-hand pour retain counter sides and action ownership.
Diff 4->5: food insert excludes bodies and implies meal-service progression; absence from crop is not disappearance.
Diff 5->6, also compared with 3->4: M now intersects A's solid geometry; fixed B/C/D orientation rules out camera reversal as the explanation.
Diff 6->7: reverse hatch angle reveals W and keeps M at front counter; unseen movement during prior shot is possible, so no additional disappearance/relocation finding.
Diff 7->8->9: empty-room dawn transition supplies elapsed time for W's movement and M's changed stool location.
Diff 9->10: closer framing retains both people on their established sides of A and continues dish handling.
Diff 10->11: W remains near rear end and her movement onto customer side is visible; M stays seated.
Diff 11->12: reverse camera changes screen order but preserves W nearer B and M nearer front on same side of A.
Diff 12->13->14: brighter empty-room insert and tight payment insert do not establish unexplained disappearance; hands cannot establish whole-body relocation.
Diff 14->15: payment-to-departure edit allows omitted walking outside; no simultaneous contradictory placement.
Diff 15->16: M continues approaching/opening truck; W's actual body and reflection occupy consistent indoor/window positions.

Diff 16->17: cut to W seated allows omitted movement from window; within shot 17, continuous counter crossing and simultaneous second W independently violate solid geometry and unique-person placement.
Coverage: all 26 supplied contact sheets inspected chronologically; selected originals and additional 4-fps frames around 01:50-01:53 resolve geometry and simultaneous presence. Audio UNASSESSED.

findings.entity: Man in brown jacket at counter
findings.description: At the cut at 00:36.458, the man holds his mug with his torso on the service/coffee-machine side of the counter, but a jeans-clad leg projects onto the stool side below its uninterrupted metal rim and wood base. His waist/seat occupies the solid counter rather than a customer stool beside it. The earlier seating shot places him normally on the customer side; the same hatch, coffee wall and windows rule out a reversed camera explaining this geometry.

findings.entity: Woman in blue shirt and white apron
findings.description: After rising from the customer-side stool, the woman carrying mugs moves directly through the counter around 01:52.25-01:52.75. Her torso is already behind the countertop while her trailing leg remains in front of the solid wood base, visibly intersecting the counter. She reaches the coffee-wall aisle without rounding either end, opening a gap or climbing over it; the movement occurs in one continuous wide shot.

findings.entity: Woman in blue shirt and white apron
findings.description: From about 01:52 through 01:55, one instance of the woman carries mugs at the near coffee-wall worktop while a second matching woman, with the same blue shirt, white apron and tied-back gray hair, wipes the far end of the counter beside the kitchen hatch. Both occupy distinct positions in the same uninterrupted wide view. The rear instance is in open room space rather than a window or mirror, unlike the earlier identifiable window reflection.
